title: Analytical performance evaluation of the On Call Plus II Blood Glucose Monitoring System
summary:
The aim of analytical performance studies is to evaluate the performance of so-called in-vitro diagnostic medical devices. In-vitro diagnostic medical devices are special medical devices, used to generate measurement results from samples taken from the human body (e.g. blood or tissue samples). The analytical performance of these devices describes their ability to correctly detect or measure a certain value.
Requirements for blood-glucose measurement devices for self-testing are described in the standard ISO 15197:2013 / EN ISO 15197:2015. In this study, the accuracy (as one aspect of the analytical performance) of the blood-glucose measurement system On Call Plus II of the manufacturer Acon Biotech (China), shall be investigated according to this standard. For this purpose, glucose measurement results will be obtained and evaluated of about 120 subjects with and without diabetes mellitus in this study. The meter and the test strips do not yet have a CE-mark, and therefore, they must not be marketed in the European Union. The results of this study shall be used to obtain the CE-mark.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Signed informed consent form
Subjects are legally competent and capable to understand character, meaning and consequences of the study.
If blood glucose values ≤ 80 mg/dl or > 300 mg/dl shall be measured after short term alteration in insulin therapy:
Subjects with type 1 diabetes and intensified insulin therapy or insulin pump therapy. 
Signature of subjects to document consent with these procedures on informed consent form
Exclusion criteria:
Severe acute disease that compromises the subject’s capability to participate in the study (at the study physician’s discretion)
Severe chronic disease with potential risk during the test procedures (at the study physician’s discretion)
Suspected lack of compliance
Other conditions which might compromise the quality of measurement results (e. g. intake of potential interfering substances, instable glucose values)
Dependence on sponsor or employees of the study site
If blood glucose values ≤ 80 mg/dl or > 300 mg/dl shall be measured after short term alteration in insulin therapy:
Pregnancy or lactation period
Subjects with type 1 diabetes, suffering from
Coronary heart disease
Condition after myocardial infarction
Condition after cerebral events
Peripheral arterial occlusive disease
Hypoglycemia unawareness
